mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 2.5% indicates accommodative monetary policy, which reduces discount rates for equity valuation and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 2.5%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 5.0%, it signals a weakening labor market that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when UNRATE > 5.0, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising inflation (CPIAUCSL > 192.0) and a stable or rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS >= 2.25%) signals an impending monetary tightening cycle that compresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances (CPIAUCSL > 192.0 AND FEDFUNDS >= 2.25), or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansion regimes (defined by housing starts above 2000.0 thousand units), the S&P 500 typically experiences negative returns as the economy approaches its peak and the risk of a downturn increases, leading to negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances when HOUST > 2000.0, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A strong labor market, indicated by monthly job gains above 132,000 thousand persons, supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of instances when PAYEMS > 132000.0, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production falls below 117.0 (index), it signals a contraction in manufacturing and services, reducing corporate profits and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when INDPRO < 117.0, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of weak retail sales (RSAFS < 347000.0 million dollars) and rising unemployment (UNRATE > 5.0) signals a broad-based economic slowdown that reduces consumer confidence and corporate earnings, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances (RSAFS < 347000.0 AND UNRATE > 5.0), or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In monetary tightening cycles (defined by the federal funds rate at or above 2.25%), the S&P 500 typically underperforms due to higher discount rates and reduced economic growth, leading to negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS >= 2.25, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
